title: Bhakti Saints Acharyas Shankaracharya
definition: Adi Shankaracharya (788–820 CE) was the pre-eminent philosopher-theologian who revived Vedic Hinduism through the Advaita Vedanta school, establishing a pan-Indian institutional framework to counter the decline of Buddhism and Jainism.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the intellectual transition from the post-Gupta period to the medieval Bhakti movement; frequently tested in Art & Culture and Medieval History sections.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Bhakti Saints Acharyas Shankaracharya.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Upanishads and Brahma Sutras
